title: Structured Data
summary: Structured data (schema.org JSON-LD in a <script type="application/ld+json"> tag) tells search engines exactly what your content is: article

sections.content: Structured data (schema.org JSON-LD in a <script type="application/ld+json"> tag) tells search engines exactly what your content is: articles, products, events, FAQs, recipes.
Rich results — star ratings, prices, FAQ dropdowns — come from valid structured data, not from visible text alone. Google's Rich Results Test validates your markup.
Key points: JSON-LD is preferred over microdata, match schema to visible content only, and one @type per entity keeps it clean.
Try this variation — change a value, predict the output, then run it:
sections.codeExample:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{ "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "Article", "headline": "My Post" }
</script>
<!-- --> experiment: modify a value above and predict the new output
